limits: Known-scenario remediation informed by the frozen prior findings; not an untouched holdout, usage statistic or user survey.
Fresh-context independent content Verification is limited to this leaf and is not a parent Audit, phase Full Audit, owner acceptance or source-corpus recertification.
Coverage uses complete returned top-eight topics and relevant expansions, not guaranteed first-snippet quality or a verified configuration SOP.
Current-state answers provide bounded checks only; no operational records, live warehouse actions or effective user settings were inspected.
QS-22 is one appropriate unspecified-setting clarification, separate from the 22 adequate substantive answers.
QS-18 retains the absent Packing replacement-LPN contract. QS-19 does not establish closed-source unpack/reopen permission or arbitrary cross-shipment repacking.
No browser, keyboard, screen-reader, representative-user or live warehouse acceptance is inferred.

method.sample: 24 frozen scenario questions derived from owner seeds and primary public workflow documentation; not usage statistics or real-user acceptance.
method.independence: Native delegated Auditor/content verifier in fresh context (fork_turns=none), independent of the topic writer and coordinator implementation work. Prior rubric/findings were read because this is known-scenario remediation. This is leaf Verification, not parent Audit or owner acceptance.
method.retrieval: One exact original question per actual loopback GET /api/search; score only the returned top eight, without query rewriting, out-of-top-eight recovery or new topic authoring.
method.inspection: Read the core explanations, ordered checks/steps, affected settings and documentary refinements of all returned topics; read complete operator guides, all 27 cited operator source-detail sets and relevant complete reviewed SQL details. Independently resolved exact cited parent nodes from retained AIM article trees for the six new operator topics. Rechecked the refreshed HTTP capture after the source-excerpt display correction and work-splitting clarification. No automatic semantic scoring was used.
method.adequate: The complete returned topic content, including expandable detail, covers the question at its answerability boundary. Current-state cases require useful bounded checks and explicit inability to know unseen current state. Adequate does not imply a direct initial search snippet, a complete configuration SOP or implemented workflow verification.
method.partial: Returned material covers a material part, but an identified requested subquestion or usable triage/configuration path remains absent.
method.missing: No substantive answer to the requested intent within the top eight; lexical matches and general descriptions do not count.
method.correctness: Inspect response scope, internal consistency and cited reviewed/source sample support. No unsupported diagnosis observed is not a proof that every underlying source statement is correct in every environment.
method.clarity: Manual plain-language reading only. Lower-ranked relevant topics and multi-topic assembly remain clarity limitations; no browser or assistive-technology acceptance.
method.clarification: QS-22 is adequate ambiguity handling because no setting is specified; its response supplies no named-setting explanation/citation and is counted separately.
method.question_file_binding: frozen_question_file_sha256 binds the compact public _project/help-question-research.json; frozen_questions_sha256 binds the unchanged canonical question set. The earlier receipt private-file binding retains its original distinct scope.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: Packing replacement-LPN validation remains undocumented in the retained sources. New error/context triage is useful, but mobile Override Pick constraints are not evidence of a Packing replacement action.
Several adequate cases require lower-ranked answers or multiple expansions; adequate content coverage does not establish first-result clarity.
Cancellation and repacking are conditional documentary triage, not authorization. Delete retains the source not-closed wording; closed-source unpack and reopen permission remain unestablished.

comparison.interpretation: Same frozen questions, new source-bound known-scenario review; no holdout or real-user acceptance claim.

results.question: What is the difference between Work Insight and Warehouse Mobile, and where should I start when a task is stuck?

judgment.answer_basis: Work Insight management is distinguished from mobile pick/putaway execution. Header/detail condition, hold and remaining-step checks provide a useful starting point for a stuck task.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the general comparison and starting checks; the actual task state remains unseen.
judgment.clarity_reason: The direct comparison is second and completion checks fifth; the first answer is a generic work overview.

results.question: I can see the work in Work Insight, but it does not appear on my handheld. What should I check?

judgment.answer_basis: The work explanation identifies authorized/default profile selection, work-type and zone/equipment eligibility and assignment ordering. Completion checks add condition, assigned user/team and release holds; the configurator details distinguish display controls from action enforcement.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for bounded triage; the active profile, current instruction eligibility and permissions are not inspected.
judgment.clarity_reason: The checks must be assembled from a general process answer, completion topic and technical configurator details.

results.question: Why does a work unit still show open after I picked everything?

judgment.answer_basis: Picking alone is separated from remaining details and putaway. Partial-pick remainder, restricted Close After Partial Pick, Skip/Pass and release holds are explained without treating the operator report as proof of completion.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for general reasons and bounded checks; no actual work unit was diagnosed.
judgment.clarity_reason: The directly relevant checklist is second, after the generic work explanation.

results.question: I cannot close this work unit. Which incomplete step or status should I look at first?

judgment.answer_basis: Work header/detail condition, open/in-process instructions, remaining pick/putaway and release holds are the first work-specific checks. Status-flow and container guidance keep work completion distinct from container closure.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the requested first checks; the actual failed action and record remain unknown.
judgment.clarity_reason: Two general process answers precede the work-specific checklist at rank three.

results.question: Can I cancel this stuck work, or will that leave inventory in the wrong place?

judgment.answer_basis: The answer distinguishes Work Insight Delete, unreleased-wave cancellation and receipt Unlocate/Cancel Check In. It preserves the source literal not-closed Delete restriction, explains allocation/status consequences and requires comparing recorded confirmations with physical location before any authorized reversal.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for bounded route-selection and movement-reconciliation triage. It cannot approve cancellation of unseen work or establish a universal repair for already executed movement.
judgment.clarity_reason: The useful route-selection answer is second and requires careful reading of several different action restrictions.

results.question: Where do I find the reason a pick failed, instead of just trying the same action again?

judgment.answer_basis: The first answer separates a validation failure from a short pick, identifies the failing field and exact error, explains verification/permission/grouping dependencies, and asks whether submission already advanced before retrying. The support checklist gathers the needed context.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the requested error-finding and safe next checks; no unseen failure cause is asserted.
judgment.clarity_reason: The first topic gives the direct diagnostic sequence; the second provides the support evidence checklist.

results.question: How do I configure which work a user can receive on Warehouse Mobile?

judgment.answer_basis: Work Profile configuration covers Authorized Users, Warehouse Access, team/equipment and zones, numbered work-type sequences, initiation/assignment and default-profile selection. Work selection distinguishes configuration explanation from an action that can write sequence values.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the general configuration explanation; effective assignments and installed navigation are not established.
judgment.clarity_reason: The full configuration answer is rank seven and the selection explanation rank six, behind several unrelated matches.

results.question: The location has fewer units than my work says to pick. What should I check before reporting a short pick?

judgment.answer_basis: Returned guidance checks verified item/location/lot/LP, quantity/unit and grouped instruction context before using the distinct short-pick reason flow. It differentiates partial from short picking and warns of serial/inventory consequences.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for bounded pre-short-pick checks; physical/system quantities and effective short-pick policy remain unseen.
judgment.clarity_reason: The directly relevant verification answer is rank four and requires the work context from other topics.

results.question: What settings decide which putaway location SCALE recommends?

judgment.answer_basis: The returned locating answers identify rule assignment, parent versus child context, ordered details, strategy, optional location selection/sort, capacity, split quantity and the two delayed-locating flags. Rule lookup alone is distinguished from locating execution.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the requested setting explanation; no container-specific effective rule is asserted.
judgment.clarity_reason: The complete explanation is distributed between ranks three, five and eight.

results.question: Why is this pallet going to an exception location when another location looks empty?

judgment.answer_basis: The new locating triage at rank two restores effective-rule/sequence and Process History decision checks, distinguishes Transaction History events, and explains why apparent emptiness does not establish eligibility. It expressly avoids inventing a universal exception-location fallback or a complete rejected-candidate log.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for bounded explanation and triage; the particular pallet decision and any unrecorded rejection remain unknown.
judgment.clarity_reason: A generic location overview still precedes the concrete decision-history triage.

results.question: How do I set a different receiving process for damaged goods and returns?

judgment.answer_basis: Dedicated Receiving Preferences can set initial hold/damaged inventory status, disposition/reason requirements and QC checks; authorized-user selection and receiving execution choices are explained. Allocation rules must separately exclude held stock.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the general configuration choice; no active preference or returned stock was inspected.
judgment.clarity_reason: Configuration details are split across the third and seventh results plus receiving/returns process topics.

results.question: Why is receiving asking for a lot or serial number for this item?

judgment.answer_basis: The receiving-specific answer identifies Item Lot Controlled, Lot Template and Serial Number flow/template controls, receipt-line supplied values, mobile versus Workbench screens, serial count/duplicate/template validation and per-container grouping prompts. It does not transfer Packing or pick-verification rules into receiving.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for general prompt triggers and screen-specific checks; the actual item/template and receiving flow remain unknown.
judgment.clarity_reason: The direct receiving-tracking explanation is third, after two broader process descriptions.

results.question: How do I stop users receiving more than the expected quantity?

judgment.answer_basis: Allow Over Receiving is tied to Original Total Quantity and the selected receiving preference, with authorized-user scope and the documented RF no-warning behavior when enabled. The answer does not substitute an unrelated PO tolerance.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the requested general setting; installed enforcement and effective user choice are not tested.
judgment.clarity_reason: The specific configuration answer is second, following the receiving overview.

results.question: How do I configure the packing station so workers get the right container choices?

judgment.answer_basis: The first answer supplies Company Access and Warehouse Access type eligibility, shipment context, employee preference/default, existing-type immutability and new-container choice. It separates wave Container Group and scan-and-weigh defaults from Packing authorization and does not invent a station-specific type list.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the documented type-choice configuration; actual access lists and user permission remain unseen.
judgment.clarity_reason: The first topic answers the requested container-choice configuration directly, with the preference topic adding detail.

results.question: I scanned the shipment at Packing, but no items appeared. What should I check?

judgment.answer_basis: Packing guidance checks the configured initiation identifier, remaining open lines, wave release, Status Info and exact row error. It preserves the basic-Packing versus configurable Status Range qualification instead of universally excluding In Picking lines.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for bounded no-items triage; actual line eligibility and current input are unknown.
judgment.clarity_reason: The complete Packing screen guide is sixth; several earlier matches focus on container closure or other flows.

results.question: What does Close Container actually do, and what happens to the container afterward?

judgment.answer_basis: Closing advances container status and prevents more packing. Auto manifesting, printing and load assignment depend on preferences/integration. The read-only model getter is explicitly distinguished from the real close action.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the requested general effect; no live close, manifest, print or load action was observed.
judgment.clarity_reason: The model-boundary topic appears first while the direct close behavior is assembled from ranks two, six and eight.

results.question: I packed all the items, but the container will not close. How do I find what is missing?

judgment.answer_basis: The first topic directs the operator to the exact close error and separately checks completed packing, pending/failed QC, preference-dependent VAS and scale/weight handling. It separates successful close from printing and other downstream effects.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for bounded closure triage; the actual blocker is not known.
judgment.clarity_reason: The first result presents the close checklist, with explicit limits and source references.

results.question: Why does Packing reject a replacement LPN even though the item looks the same?

judgment.answer_basis: The returned topic now gives useful Packing error-column and scanned-identifier triage and clearly distinguishes mobile Override Pick, including separately sourced attribute/security controls. It explicitly states that the retained evidence does not establish a Packing replacement-LPN action.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: The Packing-specific replacement-LPN action and its acceptance/rejection validation contract are still absent. The exact installed action/error contract is needed; acknowledging the gap or explaining Override Pick does not answer why Packing rejected the replacement.
judgment.clarity_reason: The useful context distinction is second. It states the evidence gap plainly but cannot supply the requested Packing validation explanation.

results.question: Can I move an item from one container to another after packing has started?

judgment.answer_basis: The answer supplies a substantive conditional path: select an individual loose-packed item, enter the quantity that should remain, preserve serial/catch-weight tracking, then pack available quantity into an eligible open container for that entity. It separates whole-child nesting and checks statuses, work and shipment context.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for bounded guidance on a permissible in-progress loose-item path. Closed-source unpack eligibility, a general reopen action and arbitrary cross-shipment moves remain unestablished and are explicitly excluded; this is not permission for the unseen container pair.
judgment.clarity_reason: The direct path is second and requires distinguishing remaining quantity from moved quantity plus item moves from nesting.

results.question: How do I configure whether packing happens on a workstation or on a mobile device?

judgment.answer_basis: Desktop assigned Packing Preferences are distinguished from mobile Work Profile Container Picking Method and Work Special Handling, plus the separate mobile Close Container screen. Screen-specific QC and create-at-close limits are retained.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the documented configuration distinction; no installed screen/menu configuration or end-to-end procedure is certified.
judgment.clarity_reason: The main comparison is rank three after an unrelated device integration topic and a type-eligibility topic.

results.question: What information should I give you when I report that a work unit or container cannot close?

judgment.answer_basis: The returned work and container checks specify action/screen, exact message, header/detail and remaining pick/putaway, release holds, QC/VAS and manual versus scale weight; printing is separately tied to trigger, document type and printer. These provide a usable combined support summary.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the requested information to report; the dedicated support-evidence topic is not returned, so the user must assemble the checklist.
judgment.clarity_reason: Several answers must be combined; there is no single returned support-report checklist for this exact question.

results.question: Can you explain this setting in plain language and show where the explanation comes from?

judgment.answer_basis: The question names no setting. The NEEDS_CONTEXT response asks for setting/field name, screen and intended outcome, with a concrete Packing Preferences example and a request to omit sensitive data.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: A named-setting explanation and citation cannot be supplied until the user identifies the setting. This is appropriate ambiguity handling, counted separately from substantive content answers.
judgment.clarity_reason: The response is a short and specific clarification; it does not invent a setting or source.

results.question: How do I configure when labels print during packing, and what should I check if closing a container prints nothing?

judgment.answer_basis: The first topic explains Auto Print at Close Yes/Prompt/No, Close Last Container document-type eligibility and unpacked-quantity condition, distinct work-start labels and user printer assignment. Other returned topics separate template/routing/selection from dispatch and physical output.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for general trigger configuration and bounded no-print checks; current printer connectivity or successful output is not known.
judgment.clarity_reason: The first answer is directly relevant and orders checks from trigger/document choice to routing and observed error.

results.question: How do I configure which items may share a container and which must stay separate?

judgment.answer_basis: The first topic explains shipment-line/item/default packing-class precedence, Container Group, Packing Criteria fields and sequences, and the full-screen Required warning/block distinction. Wave creation and RF pick/pack still require matching values.
judgment.exact_missing_subquestion: None for the general compatibility configuration; actual shipment-line criteria and deployed behavior are not inspected.
judgment.clarity_reason: The first answer explains the configuration and the important screen-specific exception in plain steps.

receipt_scope: Compact source-bound judgments. Raw response payloads and HTTP trace remain private. All 24 original questions unchanged; only their returned top eight scored. Earlier research, baseline and follow-up files were not written.
